declaration.preface: Gautam Solar Private Limited recognizes that sustainable procurement is essential to achieving our environmental, social, and governance (ESG) goals. Beyond conventional procurement criteria (price, quality, reliability, delivery), the Company is committed to managing the environmental and social risks embedded in its supply chain.
declaration.declaration: This policy applies to all procurement decisions and aims to integrate sustainability into supplier selection, evaluation, and development. It aligns with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption & Production), SDG 8 (Decent Work), and SDG 13 (Climate Action).
declaration.scope: This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and agents involved in procurement, sourcing, supply chain management, and vendor management at Gautam Solar Private Limited. It covers all categories of goods and services procured by the Company, including raw materials, components, packaging, logistics, maintenance, and indirect services.

Environmental Sustainability in Supply C: Manage environmental risks (carbon emissions, waste, water use, chemical management) alongside price, quality, and reliability
Prioritize suppliers that demonstrate best environmental practices (e.g., ISO 14001, renewable energy use, circular economy)
Reduce supply chain Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions
Social Sustainability in Supply Chain: Manage social risks (working hours, wages, health & safety, child/forced labour, discrimination, freedom of association) in procurement decisions
Prefer suppliers that provide decent working conditions, fair wages, and respect for human rights
Require suppliers to comply with applicable labour laws and international standards (ILO conventions)
Conduct social audits for high‑risk suppliers

targets.target: 100% of new tier‑1 suppliers (by spend) assessed on environmental criteria before onboarding
100% of existing tier‑1 suppliers re‑assessed on environmental performance every 2 years
90% of procurement team employees trained on environmental issues in supply chain annually
100% of new tier‑1 suppliers assessed on social criteria (wages, working hours, health & safety, child/forced labour)
100% of existing tier‑1 suppliers re‑assessed on social performance every 2 years
90% of procurement team employees trained on social issues in supply chain annually
20% reduction in supply chain GHG emissions (Scope 3 purchased goods & services) per unit of production
50% of tier‑1 suppliers by spend report their own GHG emissions annually
30% of tier‑1 suppliers by spend adopt renewable energy for ≥ 20% of their operations
100% of suppliers of packaging materials use ≥ 50% recycled or sustainably sourced content
Zero hazardous waste non‑compliance incidents among key suppliers
100% of logistics providers have a green fleet improvement plan (e.g., fuel efficiency, EV adoption)
100% of tier‑1 suppliers comply with legal working hour limits (overtime ≤ 48 hours/month or local law)
100% of tier‑1 suppliers pay at least minimum wage; 50% pay a living wage by FY 2030‑31
Zero substantiated cases of child labour or forced labour in tier‑1 supply chain
100% of tier‑1 suppliers have a formal health & safety management system (e.g., ISO 45001 or equivalent)
100% of tier‑1 suppliers provide grievance mechanisms for workers
100% of reported supplier social incidents investigated and remediated within 60 days
100% of tier‑1 suppliers (by spend) covered by sustainability assessment (environmental + social)
100% of non‑compliant suppliers (critical findings) have a corrective action plan; 90% of plans closed within 12 months
100% of procurement team members complete annual sustainable procurement training (minimum 8 hours/year)
Zero instances of procurement decisions knowingly overriding sustainability criteria without documented justifications and top management approval

responsibilities.duty: Integrate environmental and social criteria into sourcing processes, RFPs, and supplier scorecards
Ensure procurement team receives annual sustainability training
Provide technical guidance on environmental and social risk assessment
Conduct or coordinate supplier audits (environmental and social)
Track and report performance against targets
Apply sustainability criteria in all supplier selection and evaluation decisions
Provide resources and strategic direction for sustainable procurement
Review progress annually and approve corrective actions for underperforming suppliers
Raise awareness of any supplier sustainability concerns through designated channels

policy.monitoring:
The Company shall monitor progress through:

Quarterly procurement dashboards tracking supplier sustainability scores

Annual supplier sustainability surveys and audits

Training completion records for procurement team

Incident reports related to supplier environmental or social non‑compliance
policy.reviewMechanism:
This policy and its targets shall be reviewed annually by the Head of Procurement and Top Management.

Next review date: 01/02/2027

Corrective action plans shall be developed for missed targets. Suppliers that fail to improve may be subject to probation or removal.
